#779. Roseanne's Michael Fishman Reacts to Roseanne Barr's Criticism

A Lighthouse in the Dark and Fish's Call Sheet podcast host Michael Fishman revealed where he stands with Roseanne costar Roseanne Barr after she criticized his comments on the reboot's cancellation.

Michael Fishman will always have a seat at the kitchen table for Roseanne Barr.

The Roseanne alum reflected on his relationship with his TV mom after the two first starred together on the series from 1988 to 1997 and again on the 2018 reboot (which later became The Conners following Barr’s exit from the series).

“I loved Roseanne from the first moment I met her at the audition, and she and I bonded,” Fishman told E! News in an exclusive interview. “And that just grew over the course of the show.”

“I'm always going to love her,” he added, “I’m always going to care about her.”

Still, that’s not to say the current status of their relationship is without its difficulties, especially after Barr recently called out her former TV son for saying that the 2018 reboot of Roseanne had a good reason for getting cancelled following offensive social media posts from Barr.

“Look, what I'm going through in a public sense is something a lot of people are going through in the private sense, which is we all love our family members,” Fishman explained. “It does not mean we agree all the time. And the truth about that is just because you don't agree, it doesn't mean you stop loving each other.”

However, the 45-year-old noted that in those situations it’s important to “set your own boundaries” and to “have clear delineation about what you believe and what you stand for.”

“The public comments are what they are,” he continued. “The reality is I've never said anything negative publicly about her. I don't have a reason to. I'm always going to care about her.”

And regardless of how his relationship with Barr unfolds over the years, Fishman expressed that his “love for her has never wavered.”

“I’ve reached out to give her support and care about her,” he shared. “That doesn't mean we agree. And we have to be very clear where we stand and responsible for how we stand. She always knows how to reach me. There's never a time I'm going to refuse communication.”

Part of Fishman’s ability to care for Barr comes from an understanding of the human experience, a topic he touches on with his podcast A Lighthouse in the Dark.

“The world feels dark for a lot of people right now,” the podcaster admitted. “So it's an opportunity to talk with people who are doing something beautiful in the world and have really deep conversations, because I feel like we've lost an element of our ability to even disagree and to have deep conversations and connect.”

And after spending over three decades in Hollywood, Fishman is also taking a moment to put the spotlight on some lesser known figures with his podcast Fish's Call Sheet.

“Fish's Call Sheet really is about celebrating the people who make production possible and telling their stories,” he told E! News, “because rarely do we tell the stories of the people who are behind the camera.”

For a look at where more of your favorite child stars are up to now, keep reading.

JTT rose to fame playing brainy and adorable middle child Randy Taylor on Home Improvement starting in 1991. His big-screen roles that decade included voicing young Simba in The Lion King (though that's not him singing) and starring with Brad Renfro in 1995's Tom and Huck and Devon Sawa in 1997's Wild America.

He left Home Improvement in 1998 (Randy went to Costa Rica) to focus on school, but kept acting on his list of extracurriculars.

He had a recurring role on 8 Simple Rules in 2004 and in 2013 reunited with TV dad Tim Allen to direct (and appear in) several episodes of Last Man Standing.

But though JTT backed away from the spotlight to live his life, which included graduating from Columbia in 2010, Thomas doesn't need to be onscreen to cause a splash: On the rare occasions the paparazzi snap him, the sightings go viral.

Few 6-year-olds have made splashier movie debuts than Lipnicki, who went toe-to-toe with Tom Cruise in the charm department in Jerry Maguire and got almost as many memorable lines. He went on to roles in the Stuart Little films, Doctor Dolittle (voicing Baby Tiger), The Little Vampire and Little Mike, and he guest-starred on Dawson's Creek, but took a break to have a normal high school experience.

In 2017, Lipnicki opened up on Instagram about the bullying he experienced in middle school, hoping that sharing his experience could lend some comfort to others.

He was "made fun of relentlessly" by some kids who then, down the road, must have forgotten their bad behavior and tried to friend him on Facebook. "I was told I was a has-been and would never book a job again," he recalled. He started having nightly panic attacks, anticipating the next day's humiliation. Yet he had survived, adding, "I am grateful for the amazing life I have and I hope I can pass on that it DOES get better."

He's still in showbiz as an adult, starring in the 2023 Lifetime movie Secrets at the Museum and the 2026 film Primetime alongside Robert Pattinson. The L.A. native is also a black belt in Brazilian jiu-jitsu and in May 2021 he volunteered to provide additional security outside a mid-city synagogue amid a rise in anti-Semitic vandalism and harassment.

Wilson starred in Mrs. Doubtfire at 6 and Matilda at 9 before putting acting on the back burner.

The writer and activist released her memoir Where Am I Now?: True Stories of Girlhood and Accidental Fame in 2016 as well as appeared on Broad City and loaned her voice to the animated shows BoJack Horseman, Big Hero 6: The Series and Helluva Boss.

"Once, someone I'd considered a friend asked, with a big smile, 'How does it feel to know you've peaked?'" Wilson recalled in a February 2021 New York Times op-Ed about the perils of early fame for girls. "I didn't know how to answer, but now I would say that's the wrong question. I haven't peaked, because for me, The Narrative isn't a story someone else is writing anymore. I can write it myself."

Gordon-Levitt was a veteran actor by the time he starred as Tommy Solomon, a member of an alien fact-finding mission posing as an average human family, on 3rd Rock From the Sun. The show premiered when he was 14 in 1996, also the year he was seen as Demi Moore's son in the thriller The Jury.

Soon, he was the nice guy with a crush in 1999's 10 Things I Hate About You, a hustler in 2004's Mysterious Skin and the determined teen sleuth trying to find out what happened to his missing ex-girlfriend in the 2005 noir drama Brick.

He could still pass for a teen well into his twenties, but once he started playing adults, his various highlights have included 500 Days of Summer, G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra, Inception, 50/50, The Dark Knight Rises, Looper, Lincoln, Don Jon (which he also wrote and directed) and Snowden. Gordon-Levitt explored more real moments in history as a prosecutor in 2020's The Trial of the Chicago 7 and he played Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick in the series Super Pumped.

He quietly married Tasha McCauley in 2014 and they share three children.

Thanks to her preternaturally poised performance at the age of 12 in 1994's The Professional, Portman was tagged with a certain gravitas at an early age—and she's still living up to her reputation. Since her auspicious debut, she's starred in huge blockbusters (Star Wars: Episodes I through III; the Thor franchise and Avengers: Endgame), indie favorites (Beautiful Girls, Garden State), comedies (Mars Attacks!, Your Highness), intense dramas (Closer, Brothers) and apocalyptic thrillers (V for Vendetta, Annihilation).

She won the Best Actress Oscar for her turn as a ballerina who's losing her mind in 2010's Black Swan earned another nomination for channeling newly widowed Jacqueline Kennedy in Jackie. She made her feature directorial debut with 2015's A Tale of Love and Darkness, adapted from Amos Oz's autobiographical novel.

She married her Black Swan choreographer, Benjamin Millepied, in 2012 and they're parents of son Aleph and daughter Amalia. The duo finalized their divorce in 2024.

She announced her pregnancy with boyfriend Tanguy Destable in April 2026.

Jones was best known as the son of Jon Cryer's sadsack divorcé (and nephew of Charlie Sheen's playboy songwriter) on the '00s hit sitcom Two and a Half Men. In 2012, a video of Jones trashing the comedy, calling it "filth," surfaced online. The footage was from a 15-minute religious testimonial for Forerunner Chronicles, an Alabama-based Seventh-day Adventist ministry.

Jones later apologized for "showing indifference to and disrespect of my colleagues and a lack of appreciation of the extraordinary opportunity of which I have been blessed."

The actor soon left the series, but returned for the finale in 2015.

Jones, who earned a reported $350,000 per episode during his final season as a full-time cast member on the CBS sitcom, told Houston TV station KHOU that the show "was making light of topics in our world that are really problems for a lot of people, and I was a paid hypocrite because I wasn't okay with it, but I was still doing it."

Until an uncredited 2023 notch on his IMDb from the Max series Bookie, his last acting credit was Louis C.K.'s 2016 limited series Horace & Pete.

Jones attended the University of Colorado at Boulder, living what he called a "normal existence," he told People in 2016. "I got pretty doomsday with my thinking for a long time, but now I'm having fun and enjoying where I'm at," he added. "I no longer feel like every step I take is on a land mine."

Speaking of actors who could've been attached to one iconic role forever, Radcliffe has done an admirable job putting himself out there for anti-Potter parts—whether on stage in dramas like Equus and The Cripple of Inishmaan or the classic musical How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying; on film as Beat poet Allen Ginsberg in Kill Your Darlings or a flatulent corpse in Swiss Army Man; or on TV as an opioid-addicted physician in A Young Doctor's Notebook.

More recently, he wrapped up a four-season run on Miracle Workers, played the title entertainer in Weird: The Al Yankovic Story and returned to Broadway in Merrily We Roll Along.

On a personal note, Radcliffe is dad to a son with longtime partner Erin Darke.

She made her acting debut at around 6 in the Andy Griffith Show spinoff Mayberry R.F.D. and earned her first Oscar nomination at 14 for her turn as a girl being prostituted by a creepy pimp in Taxi Driver, her plight being what drives Robert De Niro's Travis Bickle to take violent action. Also in 1976, Foster starred in the original Freaky Friday, the tonal opposite of Taxi Driver, which made her more of a mainstream child star.

The serious student took a break to attend Yale, after which she re-broke through—and won her first Oscar, for Best Supporting Actress—playing a gang-rape victim who presses charges against her attackers, not realizing that she'll end up on trial in a different way, in 1988's The Accused. She made her feature directing debut with Little Man Tate in 1991, then won a Best Actress Oscar for her turn as an intrepid FBI trainee in The Silence of the Lambs in 1992.

The actress and filmmaker was honored with the Cecil B. DeMille Award for life achievement at the 2013 Golden Globes and in the last few years has done more directing for TV, helming episodes of House of Cards, Black Mirror and Orange Is the New Black. Her major big-screen credits in the 21st century include Panic Room, Inside Man, Elysium, Hotel Artemis and The Mauritanian, which earned her a surprise Golden Globe win in 2021 for supporting actress.

In real life, she's a mother of two sons with ex-partner Cydney Bernard, and she married photographer and director Alexandra Hedison in 2014.

It was natural for onetime child actress Jodie Foster to take Stewart under her wing when they played mother and daughter in David Fincher's 2002 thriller Panic Room. Like her mentor, Stewart has gone on to have a mixed-bag relationship with fame, but on a whole other Internet-enhanced level after winning the coveted, life-changing role of Bella Swan in the Twilight series when she was about 16.

"I remember her thinking there wasn't a chance I'd continue being an actor," Stewart said of Foster, talking to Stellar magazine in 2019. That, of course, had nothing to do with her talent, and everything to do with her very non-showboating personality. Stewart added, "I really love my job, but I understand why she would have thought that about me as a kid. I love her."

The actress and Chanel muse hasn't had trouble finding work since concluding the five-film Twilight saga, but other than the 2019 stab at reviving the Charlie's Angels franchise, she has preferred taking on more intimate films, including The Clouds of Sils Maria, for which she became the first American actress to win a Cesar Award (France's equivalent of the Oscars), the eerie drama Personal Shopper and the not-quite-biopics Seberg and Spencer.

After her much-chronicled relationship with Robert Pattinson ended, Stewart primarily dated women, and she married Dylan Meyer in 2025.

Several decades before he snapped his fingers and made half of Earth's population disappear, the son of actor James Brolin got his start playing the cool and exasperated but also protective and big-hearted big brother Brandon Walsh (yes, Brandon Walsh) in 1985's Goonies.

Brolin went on to do a few (dozen) movies, including Flirting With Disaster, Mimic, No Country for Old Men (which won the Best Picture Oscar and reinvigorated his career), American Gangster, W. (playing 43rd President George W. Bush), Milk (he was nominated for a Best Supporting Actor Oscar for his performance as Dan White, the San Francisco councilman who killed city official and gay rights activist Harvey Milk), Jonah Hex, True Grit, Sicario, Deadpool 2 and, of course, Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame, cloaked in CGI as super-villain Thanos, and the sci-fi epic Dune (parts one and the upcoming two).

Brolin has two children from his first marriage, to Alice Adair, after which he was married to Diane Lane from 2004 until 2013. He and wife Kathryn Boyd, whom he married in 2016, welcomed daughter Westlyn Reign Brolin in 2018 and another daughter, Chapel Grace Brolin, in December 2020.

She was barely 10 when she made her movie debut alongside Cher and Winona Ryder in 1990's Mermaids and The Addams Family, co-starring Ricci as the amusingly morose Wednesday Addams, came out the next year.

More classic 1990s moments were made with Casper and Now and Then before Ricci embarked on a career peppered with complicated characters in films such as The Opposite of Sex, Buffalo '66, Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas, Sleepy Hollow, Prozac Nation, Pumpkin and Monster, in which she played the girlfriend of serial killer Aileen Wuornos (Charlize Theron, in her Oscar-winning role).

Whatever Ricci has been up to for the past 30 years, almost all of it has been adventurous, whether it's playing a glamorous '60s-era flight attendant in the short-lived Pan Am or being chained to a radiator in Black Snake Moan, or taking on fascinating real-life women, such as ax murderer Lizzie Borden in The Lizzie Borden Chronicles, author and literary muse Zelda Fitzgerald in Z: The Beginning of Everything.

Ricci is mom to son Freddie with ex-husband James Heerdegen and daughter Cleopatra with husband Mark Hampton.

In December 2021, the Yellowjackets star welcomed daughter Cleopatra with hairdresser Mark Hampton, whom she married that October.

The Home Alone star cemented his icon status in one fell scream when he was barely 10, but he had already been hard at work since around the age of 5 in TV movies, Uncle Buck, Jacob's Ladder and more. He gave it a nearly decade-long rest after 1994's Ri¢hie Ri¢h, but the musician and painter has bounced in and out of the acting game as he sees fit, mainly in small films with big cultural footprints such as Party Monster and Saved.

After providing his voice to Adult Swim's Robot Chicken and playing a barista version of himself on The Jim Gaffigan Show, and presuming all the pandemic protocol gets sorted out, Culkin will be joining the 10th season of American Horror Story, due to premiere in 2021.

The actor is engaged to Brenda Song and they share two sons, Dakota Song Culkin (named after Culkin's older sister Dakota, who died in a car accident in 2008) and Carson, who made his public debut at his dad's Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony on Dec. 1, 2023 when he was 12 months old.

Kieran has come a long way since making his movie debut in his big brother's star vehicle Home Alone, playing Kevin McCallister's Pepsi-swilling cousin Fuller.

After growing up onscreen in the likes of Father of the Bride, She's All That, Igby Goes Down and Scott Pilgrim vs. the World, he shed all trappings of adolescent stardom with his Emmy-winning turn as acerbic media empire scion Roman Roy on Succession.

Kieran reached new heights in 2025, scooping up awards on his way to winning the Best Supporting Actor Oscar for A Real Pain.

Behind the scenes, he and wife Jazz Charton share three children: daughter Kinsey Sioux, son Wilder Wolf and their new addition, whose arrival was confirmed in September 2025 by Kieran's Succession sister Sarah Snook.

It seems as if Dakota went from playing Ally McBeal's 5-year-old self and Sean Penn's 6-year-old daughter in I Am Sam to blazing a trail as the first female employee of the New York Police Department turned private detective in the period drama The Alienist overnight. But no.

She's actually just been working her tail off for more than 20 years, turning in memorable performances in Uptown Girls, Man on Fire, Hide and Seek, War of the Worlds, Charlotte's Web, The Secret Life of Bees, three Twilight movies, American Pastoral and Once Upon a Time...in Hollywood, playing real-life Charles Manson acolyte Lynette "Squeaky" Fromme.

In addition to starring in The Nightingale with little sister Elle Fanning, she earned a Golden Globe nomination in 2025 for her performance as Marge Sherwood in the Netflix miniseries Ripley.

She may have gotten her start playing "Lucy 2 years," a younger version of her sister Dakota's character in I Am Sam, but this Fanning has blazed her own acting and style trail apart from her also-very-successful sibling.

Elle amassed the usual roles as the child of the grown-up stars in various films (Daddy Day Care, The Door in the Floor, Babel, Reservation Road) and guest-starred on multiple CSI franchises, Criminal Minds, House, Law & Order: SVU and more stuff she was probably still too young to watch when she was in it. But as a teen and into her twenties, her movie work continued to span genres, from family fare (We Bought a Zoo, Maleficent) and YA (Super 8, Twixt) to prestige dramas (Trumbo, 20th Century Women) and disturbing fantasias (The Neon Demon, The Beguiled).

Along the way, she's also played Mary Shelley in a film of the same name and Catherine the Great on the Hulu satire The Great.

The actress and singer has grown older since her star-making days on the Disney Channel's Lizzie McGuire, through which she seamlessly segued into family-friendly fare such as Agent Cody Banks, Cheaper by the Dozen and A Cinderella Story.

But, after a bit of a noticeable-role drought, Duff has excelled once again in Younger, playing the more-layered-than-meets-the-eye colleague of Sutton Foster's 40-year-old posing as a millennial in the critically acclaimed TV Land series, which is due to return for a seventh season. And though the prospect of a spin-off centered on Duff's Younger character Kelsey is exciting, O.G. fans really couldn't wait to see her return as Lizzie, though, in a reboot planned for Disney+. Unfortunately, the revival of the beloved series was shelved.

She has since starred in two seasons of  How I Met Your Father.

Duff and hockey player Mike Comrie, the father of her son, Luca Comrie, separated in 2014 after about four years of marriage and eventually divorced. She and songwriter Matthew Koma welcomed daughter Banks Violet Bair in 2018 and got married in 2019. In 2021, they welcomed another baby girl, Mae James Bair and daughter Townes Meadow Bair completed their family in May 2024.

The younger sister of Growing Pains star Kirk Cameron became crimped-hair fashion inspo for 12-year-olds everywhere playing studious eldest Tanner sister D.J. on Full House, which ran from 1987 until 1995.

She has starred in a parade of TV movies, some with major messages to send, such as 1996's No One Would Tell, based on the true story of a high school student who was murdered by her 16-year-old boyfriend after she silently suffered his abuse for months. (Yes, we're still haunted.)

But more recently, after spending two seasons as a co-host on The View, and in addition to reuniting with almost the whole Tanner family for five seasons of Fuller House on Netflix, Candace has become queen of the Hallmark Channel Christmas lineup, as well as the star of the network's Aurora Teagarden murder-mystery franchise, based on the books by Charlaine Harris.

In 2021 she celebrated 25 years of marriage to former NHL player Valeri Bure, with whom she has three children.

After playing middle sister Stephanie Tanner on Full House for eight seasons, Sweetin struggled with drug and alcohol abuse—a journey she candidly described in her 2009 memoir, unSweetined.

Three marriages between 2002 and 2016 also added to the headline fodder, as did her brief engagement to Justin Hodak, who, among his various issues, ended up violating a restraining order she had in place against him and in 2019 was sentenced to more than six years in prison for possession of a deadly weapon and falsifying evidence.

Sober since 2008, the mother of daughters Zoie and Beatrix rejoined the Tanner family for five seasons of Fuller House on Netflix and has starred in several Hallmark Channel movies, including 2019's Christmas-themed Merry and Bright and the romantic comedy Just Swipe.

It took two to play the role of Michelle Tanner, who grew from a wide-eyed baby to a precocious 6-year-old on the classic ABC sitcom Full House, after which the fraternal twins parlayed their success into a series of big-screen and direct-to-video movies, a production company, kids clothing lines, books and other products, making for a full-blown Olsen empire.

While Mary-Kate continued to act past 2004's New York Minute, joining the cast of Weeds for a season and appearing in the films The Wackness and Beastly, Ashley largely left it behind—and now both are merely fashion industry superstars as the co-founders of CFDA Award-winning The Row and Elizabeth & James.

Ashley quietly welcomed her first child with husband Louis Eisner in 2023. Mary-Kate married Olivier Sarkozy in 2015 and filed for divorce in 2020.

Before the movie stardom, the production company, the activism, the Oscar for The Revenant, the model girlfriends, the perpetual yacht life... he was homeless teen Luke, who comes to live with the Seaver family on Growing Pains in 1991. Also an actor whose baby face made him appear extra youthful well beyond his teens (he was already 16 on GP and had been acting for years), DiCaprio earned his first of six Oscar nominations (for acting) for What's Eating Gilbert Grape, and played a series of troubled kids, in A Boy's Life, The Basketball Diaries, Marvin's Room and—troubled by love, anyway—Romeo + Juliet.

He still kinda looked like a kid in Titanic, but at 22 he had reached full-on heartthrob status.

Over the past decade, DiCaprio has starred in films such as Inception, The Wolf of Wall Street, Once Upon a Time...in Hollywood, The Revenant (winning his first Best Actor Oscar) and Killers of the Flower Moon.

Moving beyond her auspicious start as Hermione Granger in eight Harry Potter films, the English actress tackled YA fare such as The Perks of Being a Wallflower and The Bling Ring, co-starred with Tom Hanks in The Circle, took on the lead as Belle in the live-action remake of Beauty and the Beast and played Meg March in Little Women. She's also dedicated her platform as a UN Goodwill Ambassador to empowering women and advocating for gender equality around the world.In addition, Watson has modeled for brands like Prada and Burberry, launched a gin company with her brother Alex Watson and enrolled in a creative writing program at Oxford.

The New Mexico native hit the jackpot his first time out, earning a Golden Globe nomination at 15 for his debut role as a sullen kid who bonds with his family's housekeeper in the 1988 TV movie Clara's Heart. But it could've all gone wrong for the star of the dramedy Doogie Howser, M.D., in which he played a 16-year-old genius doctor—and NPH pretended that it did when he gleefully spoofed himself in Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle.

But though he had a dry spell while he unwound from overdoing it as a youngster adrift in Hollywood, he did tons of theater, including three Broadway shows, and the right TV role eventually presented itself in the form of genial playboy Barney Stinson on How I Met Your Mother, for which he earned four Emmy nominations. In 2010 alone he was nominated for three Emmys and won two, for co-producing the 2009 Tonys and guest-starring on Glee.

The quadruple-threat—acting, singing, dancing, magic!—entertainer has now hosted the Tonys four times (winning the Emmy for special class programing as a producer every time), as well as the Emmys twice and the Oscars once, in 2015. He also won a Tony in 2014 for Best Actor in a Musical as the star of Hedwig and the Angry Inch.

Harris and longtime partner David Burtka welcomed twins Gideon and Harper via surrogacy in 2010 and tied the knot in 2014.

At the age of 4, she was ridiculously cute as the scene-stealing Olivia on The Cosby Show, after which she appeared in films such as The Little Rascals, Doctor Dolittle and Doctor Dolittle 2. She landed her own beloved Disney Channel sitcom, That's So Raven, in 2003, and while playing the psychic teen with inimitable fashion sense she also popped up on a bunch of the network's other productions, such as The Cheetah Girls, The Suite Life of Zack & Cody, Kim Possible and Sonny With a Chance.

Her TV work in the ensuing years after her show ended in 2007 included American Dad, Nashville, State of Georgia, The Jim Gaffigan Show, Master of None and Drunk History, and she had a recurring role on Black-ish. Raven-Symoné also spent three seasons as a co-host on The View and, in June 2020, she married Miranda Maday.

#778. AFC postpones Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia to late 2027 due to conflict in Middle East

Tournament pushed back 11 months with proposed start on 23 December

New dates with 21 January 2028 final must be approved by Fifa

The 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia has been postponed as a result of the conflict in the Middle East.

After a month of speculation following the airport attack on Riyadh’s international airport, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) confirmed on Tuesday that the tournament had been pushed back 11 months.

The rescheduled tournament is expected to kick off in the 2027 Christmas break with a 23 December start date leading up to a 21 January 2028 final.

“The organising committee for AFC Asian Cup approved to reschedule the flagship national team tournament in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions,” the AFC said in a statement.

“Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organisation and delivery of the competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.”

The proposed new dates – which fall in one of the busiest periods in European club football – must be approved by Fifa.

Saudi Arabia’s suitability to host the tournament has been a hot topic since the Riyadh airport attack by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

Other nations, who were scheduled to travel to Saudi Arabia in the November international window, have been forced to relocate their friendlies.

There was little appetite for another host nation to step in at such short notice – the tournament was slated to start on 7 January 2027 – but going ahead as planned in the current climate was fraught with risks.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

In Australia, the delayed tournament could have ramifications for coach Tony Popovic, who signed a short-term extension on the eve of the World Cup.

Popovic’s contract is due to expire after the previously scheduled January tournament, where Australia were due to face Tajikistan, Singapore and Iraq, who are coached by ex-Socceroos boss Graham Arnold.

Arnold was handed a job reprieve by the Iraqi FA last month after a form slump following the country’s first World Cup qualification in 40 years.

#777. Mee and Kenny handed first Northern Ireland call-ups

Dermot Mee and Eoin Kenny are both underage internationals with Northern Ireland

Manchester United goalkeeper Dermot Mee and Portsmouth forward Eoin Kenny have been handed their first Northern Ireland call-ups for November's final Nations League matches with Ukraine and Hungary.

Mee, 23, is a former Northern Ireland underage international and, although he has not played competitively for United this season, will add competition to NI's first choice goalkeeper Pierce Charles.

"He's been on [Under-]21s in the past so he knows a lot of the players," said manager Michael O'Neill.

"He's currently third-choice at Manchester United, he's involved obviously in their Champions League squads and I had a good chat with Johnny Evans about him. He spoke very highly of him."

Attacker Kenny, who is the son of former Republic of Ireland manager Stephen, joined Portsmouth from Dundalk in July.

The 20-year-old has made one league appearance for the Championship club, but has been handed a first call after impressing for the Northern Ireland Under-21s under Tommy Wright.

"I think this is really a reward for a strong campaign for Tommy in the 21s," added O'Neill.

"He made that move from from Dundalk to Portsmouth in the summer and it just gives us a chance to see him."

Striker Dion Charles and goalkeeper Bailey Peacock-Farrell drop out of the squad.

Sunderland defender Dan Ballard is missing after he injured his hamstring in the September win over Georgia in Tbilisi, while defender Eoin Toal, midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell are also absent through injury.

Liverpool's Conor Bradley, who has not played since January, remains a long-term absentee.

Family affair at Croke Park caps Mee's special night

Michael O'Neill's side are unbeaten at the top of League B2 and can earn promotion to the top tier for the first time.

Northern Ireland face Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday, 14 November at 19:45 GMT before they travel to Hungary in their final match on 17 November.

Both games are live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds.

The average of Northern Ireland's squad is just 23.5, and 17 of the 25 players selected are aged 23 or under.

O'Neill admitted he would rather have the likes of the injured Ballard, Bradley, McCann and Toal available, but he knows the window will be important in building depth in the squad.

"I think that the squad has to continue to develop players, they have to step in and you have to give players the opportunity to do that," he said.

"It's a very young squad and it will be stretched again. We'll be tested in these two games, but we given ourselves a good chance with obviously what we've done to date in the games."

Northern Ireland are the only side left in the entire Nations League who have yet to concede a goal in this year's competition.

Shea Charles scored a last-gasp winner in Georgia in September before a goalless draw at home to Hungary.

A 3-0 victory over Ukraine was one of the most impressive performances from O'Neill's young side, and they ended the quadruple-header with another goalless draw, this time at home to Georgia.

If Northern Ireland can top the group they would not only win promotion to League A, but they would also be all but guaranteed of a play-off for Euro 2028.

Goalkeeper: Pierce Charles (QPR - on loan from Manchester City), Conor Hazard (Wycombe Wanderers), Dermot Mee (Manchester United)

Defenders: Trai Hume (Sunderland), Tom Atcheson (Blackburn Rovers), Ciaron Brown (Oxford United), Ruairi McConville (Norwich City), Paddy McNair (Hull City), Terry Devlin (Portsmouth), Brodie Spencer (Oxford United), Michael Forbes (Dundee)

Midfielders: Shea Charles (Fulham), Ethan Galbraith (Stoke City), Kieran Morrison (Sheffield Wednesday - on loan from Liverpool), Paul Smyth (QPR), Isaac Price (West Brom), Justin Devenny (Stoke City), Jordan Thompson (Preston North End)

Forwards: Jamie Donley (Luton Town - on loan from Spurs), Ceadach O'Neill (Arsenal), Eoin Kenny (Portsmouth), Josh Magennis (Stevenage), Callum Marshall (Luton Town), Braiden Graham (Everton).

#776. Nicolas Cage Says He’s "Homeless" After Sinkhole Destroys Malibu House

Nicolas Cage described himself as "a little bit homeless" after a massive sinkhole cause major damage to his $10.5 million beachfront mansion in Malibu, Calif., in September.

Nearly two months after a massive sinkhole caused major damage to his $10.5 million mansion in California, the Leaving Las Vegas actor shared an update on his current living situation.

“I’m currently a little bit homeless,” Cage said during a Los Angeles Comic Con panel on Oct. 31. “Something happened to my house in Malibu, so I’m just sort of living in hotels."

That's why his Halloween plans with 4-year-old daughter August, who he shares with wife Riko Shibata, looked a little different this year.

"I don’t have normal trick-or-treaters that I would like to enjoy tonight," explained Cage, who's also dad to sons Weston, 35, and Kal-El, 21, from prior relationships. "I'll take my daughter out trick-or-treating somewhere in Santa Monica, but I am going to watch a movie where the director was actually nominated for Worst Director at the Razzies—called The Shining."

The Oscar winner added of the Stanley Kubrick classic, "He directed the hell out of that movie. I'm going to watch that tonight. After I put my daughter to bed, I'm going to put on The Shining."

Cage's beachfront property was one of the many houses affected by a sinkhole that opened up in September, leading local officials to declare an emergency and issue evacuation orders for residents from over 30 homes in the Malibu area.

The sinkhole—which roughly measured 60 feet wide and 25 feet deep—collapsed Cage's deck and destroyed his driveway, as well as caused a temporary gas leak in the neighborhood.

The National Treasure star had purchased the 4,000 square-foot property in 2024, 15 years after a government-placed tax lien on his real-estate holdings led to him unloading five of his homes—including a 28-room castle in Germany.

"Due to the difficult economic situation, unfortunately, I was no longer able to keep it," Cage said of his Bavarian fortress in a 2009 interview with German publication Bunte. "Even if Neidstein Castle is no longer in my possession, it will always have a firm place in my memory."

#775. From teenage limbo and Mangotsfield United to Champions League dream

Miguel Freckleton has played in the National League and Scottish Premiership, and now he is in the Champions League with LASK

From non-league to the Champions League in two and a half years.

Even in a video game, that would be a hugely successful rise for a footballer.

But for Bristol-born Miguel Freckleton, a National League winner with Chesterfield in 2024, it is a wonderful reality.

"It's been crazy. It's so hard to put into words," the 23-year-old tells BBC Sport.

Freckleton joined Austrian champions LASK in the summer after a trophy-winning one-year stint with Scottish club St Mirren.

The Jamaica international has played seven times for LASK and made his European debut on one of the club's most famous nights.

He came on in extra-time as his side overturned a 4-0 deficit against Celtic to qualify for the Champions League for the first time.

Seeing that job out reminded Freckleton, who has had three stints in the National League, of how primal the game can be at the grade above, which he experienced in the 2024-25 season with Swindon Town.

"It was tough. It felt ugly again. It felt like being back in League Two, where I just need to come on and head it and kick it," he says.

"I didn't really feel I was in the international game and there wasn't Â£30m on the line. I just felt like I was playing back when I'm a kid again. That's when you play the best, when you just feel that freedom."

The draw for the league phase then handed LASK a set of fixtures that included trips to face Liverpool at Anfield and Real Madrid at the Bernabeu.

Even now, Freckleton is still "just trying to take it in".

Freckleton was on the books at Bristol Rovers until the age of 14, opting to leave after learning of interest from Wolves and Stoke City.

He recalls an agent talking about a potential big move.

"He came across to me and my mum and said 'we know a lot of clubs want you. If you leave Rovers, we'll take you to these clubs and you'll be signed in no time'," Freckleton says.

The teenager had a Â£50,000 compensation fee on his head.

"Me and my mum being naive, we [thought] we're going to be sorted because I'm going to Wolves or wherever."

After a couple of trial sessions at Wolves coincided with Freckleton falling ill, he was left without a club.

He says he was "kind of left with nothing" - and he could see the compensation factor was likely to be off-putting.

"You're not really going to pay that money for a kid."

Freckleton was in limbo and ended up at the Bristol Inner City Academy and later attended South Gloucestershire and Stroud College (SGS).

Antoine Semenyo, who is now playing at the highest level for Manchester City and is a few years older than Freckleton, also attended SGS.

Freckleton played at a good level in youth football and managed a handful of games as a teenager for local non-league side Mangotsfield United. At the time, they were in the seventh tier of English football.

"Even at that age, he was one of the tallest players, the quickest," said Matt Curry, who coached Freckleton at the Bristol Inner City Academy and is now Mangotsfield's assistant manager.

"I certainly thought he would go on to have a career in the game."

Freckleton was a National League winner with Chesterfield in the 2023-24 season during the third of his four loan spells away from Bramall Lane

Freckleton returned to professional football in December 2021 when he joined Sheffield United.

The defender spent three and a half years with United but did not make a first-team breakthrough.

Instead, there were four loan spells. Three came in the National League with Wealdstone, Yeovil Town and Chesterfield, prior to a full year in League Two at Swindon.

Because Wealdstone were part-time, Freckleton spent hours driving between Sheffield and London to train with both of his clubs.

That loan was cut short so he could return to the Blades - theoretically, in time to feature in the FA Cup fifth round against Tottenham.

"But my papers didn't come through. I was very annoyed. I was doing so well. But that's football," Freckleton says now.

He was loaned to Yeovil, before becoming a regular at Chesterfield as they won the National League.

His last season on Sheffield United's books was also spent elsewhere, getting his first taste of EFL football with Swindon.

"I'm always grateful for these loans, even if they're bad or good," Freckleton adds. "I would not say a bad word about any of the clubs because they've helped me in my career.

"It was difficult at Sheffield United because I did want to play for them. I thought I could have done well. But there's no regrets there because the situation I'm in now, I would prefer to be in that."

Freckleton played a key role for St Mirren as they beat Celtic to win the Scottish League Cup final last December

When Sheffield United sacked manager Chris Wilder and appointed Ruben Selles in June 2025, Freckleton hoped his fortunes might change for the better at Bramall Lane.

Instead, as Freckleton remembers it, Selles was quick to tell the defender he was not in his plans.

Freckleton's mindset was clear: "I'm not wanted here no more so let's find the quickest way out and let's get the show on the road."

There was interest from League One, but St Mirren boss Stephen Robinson was "very persuasive, but also very real" and convinced Freckleton to head to Scotland.

"I went in and we played Celtic for the first game of the season. We ended up losing 1-0, but it was like, 'wow, I need to be a part of this'," Freckleton recalls.

"It was just a crazy experience of 65,000 fans in there. It was packed, everyone singing."

As well as reaching the Scottish Cup semi-finals, St Mirren won the Scottish League Cup. They met Celtic in their last match in both competitions, winning 3-1 in the League Cup final last December.

"I think winning the trophy was definitely the best feeling I've had on the pitch," Freckleton says.

"We really were underdogs. To experience it and then also come out on top against Celtic in a final was just so surreal."

After their shock Champions League play-off win over Celtic, LASK were drawn to face AEK Athens, Liverpool, Sporting, Slovan Bratislava, Bodo/Glimt, Fenerbahce, Real Madrid and Porto in the league phase

Freckleton had the winning feeling against Celtic for his new club, too, at the start of this campaign.

Two days after that historic comeback against Martin O'Neill's Glasgow giants, LASK's players and staff gathered to discover which eight teams they would face as their reward.

"The first draw was Real Madrid and then we got drew as the first team against them," says Freckleton, who joined LASK in July.

"I was just like, 'that's completed now. If I can go to the Bernabeu, wow'."

LASK have already faced AEK Athens, Liverpool and Sporting, while the Austrian newcomers have meetings with Bodo/Glimt, Fenerbahce, Porto and Real to look forward to.

"We've got some good games coming up," says Freckleton, who grew up as a Manchester United supporter.

"I'm just trying to take it in. Also, just understand that this is the reality and I'm a part of it."

Freckleton has been an unused substitute in LASK's three league phase matches so far. He hopes that run ends against Slovan Bratislava on Tuesday.

Freckleton won his first three caps for Jamaica in the extended recent international break

It has been some year for Freckleton, who has also become an international player.

The left-footed versatile defender won his first three caps for Jamaica during the September/October international break.

Freckleton is half Jamaican through his father and had started the process of gaining full citizenship almost a year before being called up.

Making his debut as a substitute against Honduras, Freckleton then started, provided an assist and played the duration in each of Jamaica's subsequent wins over El Salvador and Honduras.

It was his first time returning to Jamaica for a decade.

He could call on fond memories of summers spent there during Olympic years, watching on television as national hero Usain Bolt starred at London 2012 and Rio 2016.

"I was raring to just show the country - my country - my ability," Freckleton explains.

"I wanted to just help my country win, because I realised how important football was and how different it is when you play for your country compared to club. It's just such a bigger scale. I know Jamaica's small, but it's still such a big thing out there."

Inked into his diary is a Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Mexico over two legs later this month.

Jamaica, like LASK's home in the Austrian city of Linz, is a long way away from Freckleton's beginnings at the Bristol Inner City Academy and SGS College.

"It just proves there's no one way that works," Freckleton's former coach Curry says.

"If you're the right character and you've got the right aptitude, then you'll have a chance of making it."

#773. Pregnant Savannah Chrisley & Husband Jason Galanis Reveal Sex of Baby

Shortly after announcing their pregnancy and marriage, Savannah Chrisley and husband Jason Galanis shared in a sweet sex reveal video that they're expecting a baby boy.

Savannah Chrisley is unlocking a new chapter.

The Chrisley Knows Best alum is going to be a boy mom, as she and husband Jason Galanis shared they are expecting a son.

"My sweet miracle boy… you are everything we prayed for and more," Chrisley wrote on Instagram Nov. 2 alongside a video of her slicing into a cake with blue icing inside. "The past few days have reminded me just how cruel this world can be. But no amount of hate could ever overshadow the joy of loving you. You are a MIRACLE."

"My precious baby boy, your daddy and I will spend the rest of our lives protecting you, praying over you, and loving you beyond measure," she vowed in her caption. "We may not be able to shield you from every bit of darkness in this world, but we promise to raise you to be a LIGHT in it."

The 29-year-old added, "You are already our greatest blessing, our answered prayer, and the sweetest chapter of our lives."

Chrisley first revealed she was pregnant in an Oct. 27 Instagram post, praising Galanis, who she hadn’t named at the time, for being “my protector. My fiercest fighter. My most loyal person. My lover. My safe place.”

“For the first time in a long time, I feel safe,” she said. “I feel fulfilled. I can finally exhale. I found my forever in you. And just when I thought my heart couldn’t hold any more love, God gave us our sweetest blessing yet… we’re having a BABY!”

And even before the pair welcomed their little one, the Unlocked podcast host was able to get a preview of the kind of dad Galanis would be.

“J, watching the way you already love and protect our baby before he/she has even entered this world has made me fall in love with you in an entirely new way,” she explained. “Not a single doctor’s appointment missed. Constantly caring for me, talking about our baby, and reminding me how beautiful my growing bump is.”

The reality star added, “I thank God every day that this baby gets to call you Daddy.”

Though Chrisley didn’t confirm her baby daddy’s identity, multiple outlets reported that “J” was Galanis shortly after her pregnancy announcement.

Days later, Chrisley confirmed she and Galanis, 56, were married, privately tying the knot in the Cayman Islands earlier this year.

"We ended up getting married in the Cayman Islands in July," Savannah said on the premiere episode of Golden Tate's The Golden Ticket YouTube series released Nov. 1. "We did everything there, but we haven't filed it here—or else then it would be public record."

And while they still plan on having a larger wedding celebration in May, she shared that the couple’s priority was welcoming their family’s new addition, which Chrisley called “such a gift.”

"Like, I can say, 'Oh, being pregnant sucks,' or, 'It's not fun,'" she said, "but when you feel your baby kick and you literally see your pants move because you kicked so hard, you're like, 'That's what it's all for.'"

Plus, she shared that stepping into motherhood presents the perfect opportunity to “raise a kid up right, teach them the right ways, make a difference, be different from other people.”

For Chrisley—whose parents Todd Chrisley and Julie Chrisley were released from prison last year—she can’t imagine anything better.

"It's the biggest blessing, alright?” she added. “It's nothing. I can be large and in charge for a few months. I'll be fine. I might not be happy about it, but I'm good."

Keep reading for a closer look at the Chrisley family tree...

Todd Chrisley is the patriarch of the Chrisley family.He was born in Georgia in April 1969 and raised in South Carolina. He and first wife Teresa Terry welcomed daughter Lindsie Chrisley in 1989 and son Kyle Chrisley in 1991 before splitting a few years later. After their breakup, Todd wed Julie Chrisley (born in South Carolina in January 1973) in 1996.Together, they added to their family with the births of kids Chase Chrisley, Savannah Chrisley and Grayson Chrisley and the adoption of Kyle's daughter Chloe Chrisley. They also went through challenges, including Julie's 2012 breast cancer battle (she's now cancer-free).As Todd said on the premiere of Chrisley Knows Best—a show that followed the family's ups and downs as well as their rich lifestyle in Atlanta and later Nashville—he made "95 percent" of their money through his real estate business before entering reality TV. As for Julie, she was working at a bank when she started dating Todd. Chrisley Knows Best ran from 2014 to 2023 and led to spin-offs like Growing Up Chrisley and What's Cooking With Julie? as well as other media ventures like the family members' podcasts.In 2022, Todd and Julie were convicted of fraud and tax crimes, and they were originally sentenced to 12 and seven years in prison, respectively (with him being held in Florida and her being behind bars in Kentucky). The couple pleaded not guilty.In May 2025, President Donald Trump pardoned Todd and Julie and they were released from prison.

Born in September 1989, Lindsie is Todd's eldest daughter from his marriage to Teresa.She attended Georgia State University, where she met now-ex husband Will Campbell. They wed in 2012, and she graduated and gave birth to their son Jackson that December. Two years later, Chrisley Knows Best premiered.Lindsie appeared on the series for five seasons, where viewers saw how Todd and Will didn't get along. She and Will filed for divorce in 2016, and she left the show in 2017.In the years following, there was public fallout between her and her family. It wasn't until 2022 that Lindsie, Todd, Julie and Savannah reunited publicly on crossover episodes of their podcasts.However, their reunion was short-lived. In a 2025 episode of her podcast The Southern Tea, Lindsie said she hasn't seen her dad "in quite some time." The following month, she confirmed she's also estranged from her siblings."We can live in the same space doing the same things and not necessarily agree or align and it’s no hate, it’s no ill will," Lindsie said on Catelynn Lowell and Tyler Baltierra’s podcast, Cate & Ty Break It Down in 2025. "We just don’t serve each other in each other’s lives."In May 2026, Lindsie was arrested on suspicion of DUI, attempting to elude police, improper passing and reckless driving and speeding."I got pulled over speeding past a car on a two lane road," she told TMZ, "because they almost hit an animal and I was trying to miss hitting them and whatever the animal was."

Kyle, born in August 1991, is Todd’s eldest son from his former marriage to Teresa. In November 2012, he became father to daughter Chloe, whose mother is his ex Angela Johnson. But in 2016, Todd and Julie adopted Chloe.While Kyle appeared on only the first season of Chrisley Knows Best (aside from a brief cameo in 2021), his past arrests and rocky relationship with his family (which involved them being estranged and reuniting at various points in time) continued to make headlines. He’s also spoken candidly about his mental health journey and battle with addiction, sharing in a 2019 Facebook post that he's sober.In 2021, Kyle wed Ashley Nelson and became a father to her kids Haiden and Mackenzie.As for where Kyle stands with Todd and Julie, he expressed his hope to reconnect with them after their return from prison."I know they can't wait to get home and just be with family," he told E! News in May 2025, "and I'm going to remain hopeful that another reconciliation is possible."

Chase is the first child Todd welcomed with wife Julie, arriving in June 1996.In addition to appearing on Chrisley Knows Best with his parents and siblings, the entrepreneur co-starred on Growing Up Chrisley with his sister Savannah from 2019 to 2022. Chase was previously engaged to Emmy Medders. But after breaking up and getting back together, they officially parted ways in 2023.After Chase's parents entered prison, he spoke about how he and his siblings came together."We've definitely gotten a lot closer," he told Extra in 2023. "When you get hit with something like this, I feel like a lot of people either separate and go their own ways or they cling together, which is how we were raised. We've clung together and we're still fighting."Chase had his own run-in with the law in January 2025, when he was arrested in Atlanta on a simple battery charge for allegedly becoming "really drunk" and slapping a bar manager after being asked to leave, according to police records obtained by E! News. His lawyers told People that "this incident has been entirely blown out of proportion.""He did not assault anyone," they added. "Chase was trying to close out his tab and leave. We will be independently investigating the situation."

Todd and Julie welcomed daughter Savannah in August 1997.Early in her career, she competed in the pageant world—winning Miss Tennessee Teen USA in 2016 and vying for the Miss Teen USA crown later that year. However, her time in the limelight didn't end there as she went on to appear on several reality and competition shows, including Chrisley Knows Best, Growing Up Chrisley, The Masked Singer and Special Forces: World's Toughest Test. Savannah is also a real estate agent in Tennessee, the founder of Good Girl RX and host of the podcast Unlocked.In her personal life, Savannah got engaged to hockey player Nic Kerdiles in 2019. However, they broke up the following year, and he died after a motorcycle crash in 2023. She later dated Robert Shiver; however, she confirmed their split in April 2025 after about two years together. Savannah obtained custody of her brother Grayson and sister Chloe while Julie and Todd were in prison and advocated for her parents' release.After Trump pardoned Julie and Todd and they were released from prison, Savannah posted footage from their return home, including one that read "Reunited and it feels so good."In October 2026, Savannah announced she's engaged—with her fiancé revealed as Jason Galanis, who served time in the same prison as Todd before receiving his own presidential pardon in 2025—and that they're expecting a baby.

Grayson is Todd and Julie's youngest son.Born in May 2006, Grayson entered the spotlight when Chrisley Knows Best premiered eight years later. He's now a student at the University of Alabama—and yes, he gets recognized on campus."It's been insane," he said on a February 2025 episode of Savannah's podcast Unlocked. "It's more than it's ever happened here."After Julie and Todd went to prison, Savannah gained custody of Grayson and Chloe."I’m not their mom. I’m not their dad. I’m their sister and I get to love and guide them through life," the podcaster wrote on Instagram in July 2023. "Being a bonus parent is TOUGH…no one could ever add up to their parents. But these kiddos have shown me so much love, patience, grace, understanding, and appreciation! Helping to raise these two kiddos is the hardest but most rewarding job I will ever have."And Savannah's bond with Grayson grew even stronger."Many people look at our situation and think, 'She saved him,'" she wrote on Instagram for his 18th birthday in May 2024, "but little do they know… YOU saved ME."

Todd and Julie started out as Chloe's grandparents after his son Kyle fathered the child with ex Angela Johnson in November 2012. However, they adopted her four years later.“My heart!” Julie wrote on Instagram in February 2018. “This child brings so much happiness to our family. What did we do without you?”Fans watched Todd and Julie raise Chloe—or CoCo as her family calls her—on Chrisley Knows Best. But after the couple entered prison, Savannah took over as her guardian.“Watching her grow has been the biggest blessing of my life… she has QUITE the personality!” Savannah wrote on Instagram for Chloe’s 11th birthday in November 2023. "I wish I had her humor. I wish I had her carefree spirit. I wish I had her heart. She is everything that I hope to be one day! There is not a day goes by to where she doesn’t reach me something new. Because of her… we are all better people! I love you sweet girl! KEEP SHINING! NEVER GIVE UP! And ALWAYS KNOW… I AM HERE!”After it was announced that Trump was pardoning Todd and Julie, Savannah shared Chloe’s reaction. "Chloe I think is still in shock, and she doesn't want to get her hopes up because she feels like something bad's going to happen," she said on a May 2025 episode of News Nation. "But I'm excited to be going to get my dad and bringing him home to her."

Faye Chrisley—a.k.a. "Nanny"—is Todd's mom."I am blessed beyond measure that God chose you to be my mother," he wrote on Instagram for Mother's Day in 2021. "I love you more than you will ever know and you fill my heart with love, hope, faith and confidence."Born in September 1944, Nanny grew up in South Carolina. She married army veteran Gene Chrisley, and they welcomed sons Todd, Randy Chrisley and Derrick Chrisley, the latter of whom died when he was a baby. Gene also passed away in 2012.While on Chrisley Knows Best, Nanny captured fans' hearts with her humor, fun times with sister Frances (who died in 2022), dating adventures and advice. And whether she was hitting the casino, raising a glass of wine or spending time with family, she proved to viewers she knows how to have a good time.However, Nanny has gone through hard times too. In addition to Todd and Julie's convictions, Nanny was diagnosed with bladder cancer in 2021. But two years later, she shared she had overcome her health battle."I’m in remission, thank God," Nanny said on a 2023 episode of Lindsie's podcast The Southern Tea, per People. "I’ve been out moving around, doing the best I can."Doing the best she can has been Nanny's approach to life in general."The world don’t always give you a good deck of cards to play with, so you play with them the best you can," she said on Savannah's podcast Unlocked in 2023. "You get up, brush yourself off and keep going."

#772. ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace

The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind

It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles.

The journalist and lecturer Dr Victor Ademola was in Morocco the day of the defeat. “It was a very difficult evening,” he says. “Some players were visibly emotional while others appeared to be processing what had just happened. I saw players crying as they got on to the team bus while some sat alone or remained on their phones, looking very sad.”

The blow of missing out on the World Cup in Brazil next year came only a few days after they were eliminated from Wafcon at the quarter-final stage by Cameroon – only the semi-finalists qualified for the World Cup automatically, hence Nigeria ending up in that ill-fated playoff.

“What struck me most was the weight of what the result represented,” Ademola says. “These players knew the history of the Super Falcons and understood that this was not simply another defeat. There was a sense of disappointment, disbelief and heartbreak.”

The loss is not only historical but consequential. Nigeria will miss out on developmental funding with next year’s prize fund expected to rise from the previous tournament four years ago. In 2023 the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, pledged to equal the men’s and women’s tournaments prize funds by 2027. The figure for the men’s World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico was $727m (roughly £539m). Recent news suggest Fifa will miss out on its target but it is nevertheless a blow for Nigeria not to be involved.

Janine Anthony, the African women’s football journalist, says the stakes for the Super Falcons were especially high as “women’s football does not have the luxury of not being at a World Cup”. Anthony adds: “A spot at the World Cup is the ultimate window and it’s a dream to be able to represent your country at any stage, whether it’s in music or football. For women’s football, the World Cup is such a commercially marketable vehicle. The Super Falcons team were one of only seven teams that had been to every World Cup, [and] the only African team. Now that’s gone.”

Anthony says that despite the Super Falcons’ success they are treated as an “absolute afterthought” in terms of the domestic leagues, management and preparation. The lack of preparation games proved problematic in Morocco, she suggests, manifesting itself in a lack of cohesiveness in most games. The then coach, Justine Madugu, frequently changed the starting XI throughout the tournament.

Before the tournament the team played two games against Senegal, who have never qualified for the World Cup, whereas before the 2025 edition they had three friendlies, against France, Cameroon and Portugal. “Imagine if they had more games to prepare,” Anthony says. “Then they could have probably done all the tweaking from a tactical perspective. The Nigerian Football Federation absolutely failed to capitalise on the Wafcon being moved to July.”

The landscape of African women’s football is changing, and Morocco are the only country from the continent who played in the 2023 World Cup who are guaranteed to be at next year’s tournament. South Africa are going into the inter-continental playoffs which start this month, and Nigeria and Zambia are out.

At the Wafcon, Malawi and Cameroon emerged as the standouts. It was Malawi’s debut at the tourmanent and the team gave a stellar performance with the attacking skill of the Chawinga sisters, Tabitha and Temwa, standing out. They will play at their first World Cup. The winners, Cameroon, were unexpected competitors at Wafcon, only qualifying after the Confederation of African Football expanded the tournament from 12 to 16 teams.

The Super Falcons’ absence from the World Cup next year is just the latest setback in a long line of disappointments. The men’s team have failed to qualify for two World Cups in a row while the under-17 men’s team have not reached the World Cup since 2019 or even Afcon since 2023. There have been signs of progress for the the under-20 women, who beat England 3-0 to reach the quarter-finals at their World Cup in September, but they then promptly lost against Colombia 1-0.

Players and coaches have long spoken out and protested against unpaid allowances and bonuses by the Nigerian Football Federation. The Super Falcons have staged numerous sit-ins and training boycotts to protest against the conditions, including at the Wafcons in 2004, 2016 and 2022 as well as the 2019 World Cup.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

The NFF is under investigation by the country’s department of state services for an alleged misuse of a 17bn naira (£9.5m) fund issued by the government in 2024 to address outstanding payments owed to players and staff of the national teams, according to local media. The NFF did not comment when contacted by the Guardian regarding the accusations.

Nigeria’s president, Bola Tinubu, is unhappy about the situation. “Nigerian football must undergo far-reaching changes to strengthen governance, administration, stakeholder representation, player development, domestic competitions and accountability,” he said in August.

That came shortly after Ibrahim Gusau resigned as NFF president along with several other board members. The NFF was scheduled to hold elections in September but they were suspended. They are now expected to take place following reforms made in consultation with Fifa and Caf.

What does the future hold for the Super Falcons? Anthony hopes for more investment, accountability and a bridge between veteran players and the current team on an administration level. “We can only hope that there is the understanding that the Nigerian fans are really disappointed and sad that their national teams aren’t bringing the joy that Nigerians are used to as a football loving nation,” she says. “We can only hope that the Super Falcons can finally be given the respect they’ve always deserved.”

#771. How Arteta is getting the best from Rice

Rice is a rounded midfielder, but could be more selfish - Murphy

The lighthouse? One of the best midfielders that Arsenal have ever had? A future England captain?

These are just some of the things that have been said about Declan Rice.

The Arsenal midfielder has hit the ground running this season and the praise has come rolling in.

The 27-year-old has been one of Arsenal's standout performers as they have stormed to the top of the Premier League and was player of the match as the Gunners beat Liverpool on Sunday.

He already has five assists in the league this season, the most of any player, and all of them have come from open play after having his role changed by Mikel Arteta.

Rice has scored and assisted 55 goals since joining the Gunners in 2023, a somewhat underrated output for a player whose energy is so commonly spoken about as his main strength.

Arteta said he had a talk with Rice at the beginning of the season and told him he is no longer Arsenal's "lighthouse" - a name he had given him - and that he expected more this season.

The Arsenal manager said he will reveal Rice's new nickname at the end of the season but that chat clearly stuck with Rice, who referenced the conversation after the Liverpool win.

"The way I've started this season is the position that suits me the most. I've played in eight, I've played six, I've played everywhere in midfield. But what suits me the best and the conversation I had with the manager at the start of the season, I've done well but he believes I can still do more and he's drilled that into me." Rice told Match of the Day.

"This season I've really tried to attack that part going forward, trying to come up with assists, create chances, create moments.

"But being behind the ball as well, linking the play, being involved with all aspects for me is my best position. Whatever the manager decides, I'll do."

Rice has previously said he likes to play three games a week to pick up a rhythm of a season but, after 55 games for Arsenal last season, neural hamstring pain and a World Cup run to the semi-finals with England, the amount of games started to take its toll.

However this season, with the signing of Bruno Guimaraes, Rice has afforded a break for the games in the EFL Cup - and he was rested by England in the last international break.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher called him "world class" after his latest dominant performance.

"He's one of the best midfield players Arsenal have ever had," Carragher said.

"They've obviously had some great ones. He's right up there with the best of them. He's the best midfield player in the Premier League by a long way. It's not even a debate."

Kai Havertz said that "90%" of his winning goal against Liverpool belonged to Rice, such was the energy of Rice and quality of the ball he put in to assist the German.

Arsenal's midfield has rotated more this season, with opposition managers mentioning how difficult it is to defend against.

Rice has at times anchored the base of the Arsenal midfield but, with the addition of Guimaraes, as well as playing with Myles Lewis-Skelly, he has been allowed to also take up positions higher up the pitch.

Rice has still started all of the Premier League and Champions League games, helping Arsenal to make a strong start to the season.

Talks have been ongoing about a new contract, with Arteta saying Rice "wants to continue here for the long term and it will be a matter of time when we resolve that".

#770. Boy arrested following Bradley Lowery taunt

Black Cats fan Bradley died at the age of six in 2017

A 14-year-old boy has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and subsequently bailed, after a video on social media appeared to show a Coventry City fan taunting opposition Sunderland fans with a photo of Bradley Lowery.

Sunderland fan Bradley, who died aged six in 2017 after being diagnosed with a rare childhood cancer, captured the hearts of the football world.

The 14-year-old handed himself into West Midlands Police, who said they were investigating the incident.

The Sky Blues added they were also investigating the footage from Saturday's Premier League match and Bradley's mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement.

"So much of Bradley's short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face," she posted on Instagram.

"To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt."

Her "beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate," Lowery said in an update through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children with cancer.

She added she did not want hatred directing at the teenager involved, but instead wanted him to learn from his actions.

A spokesperson for the club said: "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland [on Saturday]."

"The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action."

West Midlands Police added they understood the upset the video had caused and were keeping Bradley's family updated as the investigation continued.

#769. DWTS' Disney Elimination Is Not the Fairest of Them All

Dancing With the Stars bid a fond farewell to one couple on the Nov. 2 Disney Night episode as the duo enjoyed their final magical moment on the dance floor.

Despite a magical evening, one couple had to leave the happiest ballroom floor on Earth during the Nov. 2 Disney Night episode of Dancing With the Stars.

Although they wowed the judges with a Paso Doble set to “Satisfied” from the musical Hamilton, Julia Stiles and her partner Ezra Sosa would no longer be in the room where it happens.

“It's been an incredible experience. I pulled things out of myself that I didn't realize were there,” Stiles said through tears following the elimination. “And Ezra is just an amazing person. I'm going to be sad not to see him every day.”

Sosa was equally downhearted to be saying goodbye, especially because he had seen Stiles grow so much as a dancer throughout the experience.

“Just to see your growth in and outside the ballroom has been an absolute honor,” he told the Save the Last Dance actress. “I'm so lucky that I got to share this experience with you. I love you so much.”

Still, plenty of couples had no worries for the rest of their days during the evening, as Harry Shum Jr. and partner Jenna Johnson received a perfect score for their jazz routine to “Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious” from Mary Poppins, as did Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy for their quickstep to “Be Our Guest” from Beauty and the Beast.

Amber Glenn was also ready to shout it from the mountaintops with her partner Pasha Pashkov as the two quickstepped to “A Star Is Born” from Hercules, as Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach let the audience be part of their world, dancing a samba to “Under the Sea” from The Little Mermaid.

Disney’s Broadway adventures also got a moment on the dance floor, as Tatyana Ali and her partner Jan Ravnik took a page from the Broadway book, dancing a contemporary routine to “Easy as Life” from the Disney-produced musical Aida.

Disney Night was certainly a wonderland away from last week’s Horror Movie Night, where the dancers said goodbye to two couples: Savannah Bananas baseball player Jackson Olson and his partner Emma Slater, as well as Bachelor Nation alum Tyler Cameron and pro dancer Sharna Burgess.

And luckily, the dance pros would always have a friend in their partners, with Burgess raving to E! News how close she and Cameron had become outside the ballroom.

"There's been a lot of things happening in my life that he's been an incredible friend through. He's so grounded for his age. He's so well beyond his years that he surprises me sometimes with his wisdom and his depth,” she shared. "I found an amazing human that I just want to keep in my life."

For a look at all the stars hoping to visit a whole new world as the winners of the famed Mirrorball trophy, keep reading.

You won't hate this news—the 10 Things I Hate About You star will be saving the last dance for her pro partner.

The celebrity chef couldn't cha-cha-chop away the competition and was eliminated during the Sept. 22 episode.

What did you miss on Glee? The actor taking his musical talents to the dance floor.

Sadly, the former '90s teen heartthrob did not MMMBop his way to the top of the leaderboard on season 35. He and his pro partner were axed from the competition on Sept. 29.

The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air actress will be bringing her fresh moves to the dance floor.

Twenty years after starring in Step Up, the dancer is stepping up to the challenge.

The 2026 Olympic figure skater will take her skills from the ice to the ballroom.

The Team USA Paralympic track and field athlete will show off his athleticism on DWTS.

Though her sister Brooks Nader was the fifth star to be eliminated on season 33, the Love Thy Nader star said goodbye to the competition after her debut episode on Sept. 16.

The comedian, also known as Fibula on social media, is ready to earn more applause on DWTS.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star followed his wife Whitney Leavitt's footsteps after her season 34 appearance, but he bid farwell to the season 35 competition during the Sept. 15 premiere.

The Bachelor Nation star is trading in roses for rumbas.

The Savannah Bananas baseball player is stepping up to the plate, bringing his dance moves from the diamond to the ballroom.

The Jimmy Kimmel Live! star was ready to learn some new moves, but his time on DWTS was cut short on Oct. 13.

Even though Summer House star had fans screaming "bravo," she was eliminated from the competition on Oct. 6.

The Love Island U.K. alum is hoping her love for DWTS doesn't betray her as she manifested this experience.

#768. West Ham turn to Scott Parker after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo as head coach

West Ham intent on instant return to Premier League

Nuno took over from Graham Potter in September 2025

West Ham are poised to appoint Scott Parker as their manager after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo. Parker has been out of work since leaving Burnley last season but there is optimism he will be in place when West Ham visit Cardiff City on Wednesday.

The club kept faith with Nuno after their relegation from the Premier League last season but patience has snapped with the side eighth in the Championship after the 3-1 defeat by West Bromwich Albion last Saturday.

Nuno struggled to get his ideas across after taking over from Graham Potter in September 2025. He had 33 games to save West Ham from relegation but his tactics were poor, his team selections were confusing and his signings have not worked out.

West Ham are intent on an instant return to the top flight and want to get their automatic promotion hopes back on track. Parker is a former West Ham player and his backroom staff is expected to include his former teammate Mark Noble.

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track,” a club statement said.

“Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also departed. West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the club, and wish them all the very best for the future.”
